normalized.prelim_summary: This 2008 Porsche Cayman S 6-speed has well-documented service history and desirable options, but carries some concerns: a reported minor accident, six prior owners, and unresolved buyer questions about possible bore scoring that the seller never had formally inspected. The auction ended with a high bid of $19,250 against reserve not met, down from the seller's own $22,500 purchase price a year earlier.

critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope images, specialist report or engine-rebuild invoices are mentioned for this 109k-mile M97 3.4. The seller's 'drives so well, sounds even better' is not evidence of clean cylinder walls. Per profile this is a bonus, not held against the car, but it is the central engine-risk question on an S.
No DME over-rev report is mentioned in the listing or comments.

Listing states water pump and thermostat 2019, AOS replaced June 2026, intake manifold gaskets and plugs 2023, and oil changes about every 5k miles. Carfax shows 32 service records, but no invoices are attached here. Coolant pipe and radiator condition are not mentioned.

documentation.rationale: Identity half is solid: VIN, a build sheet in comments, a Carfax with 32 service records, BaT sale history, and cold-start and driving videos. Maintenance half is partial: dated work is itemised in prose but no invoices are shown, there is no borescope or DME report, and no repair records for the 2015 damage.

condition.rationale: Photos show tidy paint, a clean cargo area, mildly worn but intact seats, and a dry-looking rear underside. Recent AOS, bearings, brake fluid and oil are claimed. Open items: engine bore condition at 109k on an M97 3.4 is unknown, clutch is unknown, and the prior listing's airbag light and suspension rattle are unaddressed.

price_value.rationale: The current bid is not meaningful. The likely hammer sits around the lower part of the $23.6k-27.8k fair-value band, for a 109k-mile S with six prior owners, a reported accident, no borescope and an unknown clutch. The same car sold for $22,500 at 98k a year ago with disclosed faults.

mission_fit.rationale: A manual 987 Cayman S is a named keeper choice, but the profile accepts the 3.4 S only with unusually strong engine due diligence, which this listing lacks. A keeper purchase also competes with cash preservation in accelerated_bridge mode.

logistics.rationale: Woodinville, WA is a fly-and-drive distance from Carmel, and the Seattle area has Porsche specialists for a pre-auction PPI. The seller is responsive, but PPI access is not stated, and the auction close (Oct 24) limits the time available.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Six-speed manual S with Carbon and Preferred Plus packages, Bose, Bi-Xenon and 19in SportDesign wheels, in black over black/stone gray. Desirable spec, tempered by six prior owners and a non-original head unit.

evidence.mission_note: A manual 987 Cayman S fits the future-keeper list, but the profile accepts the 3.4 S only with unusually strong engine due diligence, and this 109k-mile, six-owner car currently offers none. It also does not solve the near-term bridge need and competes with cash preservation.
evidence.rationale: The listing firmly establishes identity: VIN, build sheet, six-speed manual S, and a mileage history (98k at the Oct 2025 BaT sale, 108,882 now) that is internally consistent. It discloses a 2015 Carfax minor-damage entry and six prior owners, and itemises dated service including AOS, rear bearings, brake fluid and water pump, all in listing prose without attached invoices. The prior BaT listing for this same VIN disclosed an active airbag light (code 8016), a suspension rattle and a detached carbon trim piece; the current listing does not say whether any were addressed. The core engine question for an M97 3.4 at 109k miles, cylinder bore condition, has no borescope, no DME over-rev report and no compression/leakdown data. Clutch and flywheel history, tire date codes and coolant-pipe condition are also undocumented. The photos support good cosmetic condition and a dry-looking rear underside but cannot speak to engine health. The likely hammer is near the low end of the mileage-adjusted fair-value band; the prior sale of this car was $22,500.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller before Oct 24 asking for the airbag-repair invoice, the AOS/water-pump/bearing receipts and a DME over-rev printout, and request permission for a Seattle-area Porsche specialist PPI with a full borescope before bidding.
